terms.gloss: stick to one’s opinion, not give way
terms.grammar: stō, stāre, stetī, statum, with in and the ablative
terms.comment: Latin stands in its opinion: in sententiā stō, I stick to my guns.

evidence: Cic. Rosc. Com. 18.56: perstat in sententiā Saturius (Lewis & Short)

terms.grammar: the opinion is the subject: “my decision stands”

sources: Lewis & Short: sto
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 108.
